sections.html:
Gwinnett is a core county of metro Atlanta, with Lawrenceville as the seat and Peachtree Corners as the most populous city. Fifteen cities lie wholly or partly inside it, among them Duluth, Lilburn, Norcross, Snellville, Sugar Hill and Suwanee. Several cross into a neighboring county, so look at the parcel record to see which commissioner sends your bill.

Gwinnett County Public Schools serves most of the county. Households within Buford city limits belong to the separate Buford City School District. Which district and city apply depends on where the parcel sits, and both belong in your description of the property. Workers average a 32.8-minute trip to work, which buyers ask about.

The county held 957,062 people at the 2020 census. The July 2025 estimate is 1,018,099, up 6.3%, and housing units number 356,091.

sections.h2: Which Gwinnett County office handles which tax question?
sections.html:
Several offices share the work. The commissioner sends bills and takes in and passes on the money, with no part in deciding the amount. The Board of Assessors sets values, while millage rates come from the commissioners, the school board and each city.

  • Property tax (tax commissioner): 770-822-8800, tax@gwinnettcounty.com, open weekdays 8 to 5.
  • Board of Assessors, real property: 770-822-7200; personal property: 770-822-7220. Values and appeals go through Gwinnett-Assessor.com.
  • Board of Commissioners, county millage rates and fees: 770-822-7000.
  • Board of Education, school millage: 678-301-6200.
  • Clerk of Court, deeds and liens: 770-822-8100.

The commissioner's brochure page is the best single reference. Mail payments to P.O. Box 372, Lawrenceville, GA 30046.

These dates are typical and can change, so the bill in your hand outranks any chart.

  • January: mobile home bills go out, with payment due April 1.
  • April 1: returns on business tangibles, aircraft and watercraft reach the Board of Assessors.
  • May and June: the Annual Notice of Assessment goes out, and appeals must be filed within 45 days of its date.
  • July and August: taxing bodies set millage rates through advertised, public processes.
  • August or September: real and personal property bills are mailed and also posted online.
  • October or November: payment comes due.

The Board of Commissioners can change the due date each year, so read your own bill. Personal property worth more than $20,000 combined is taxable, and a late or unreported return may draw a 10% penalty. A late mobile home bill adds a 10% penalty, then 1% interest each month after June 1.

Paying online by check costs nothing, and online card payments add a convenience fee. Other options are the drop boxes open around the clock at all five tag offices, a mailed check to the Lawrenceville box, or a visit to any tax commissioner office. Cash must be handed over in person, and the county asks that none be mailed.

A few cities run their own property billing. The commissioner covers mobile home, heavy-duty equipment and timber tax in every city, but real property inside a city that bills on its own is a question for that city's tax department.

Homestead exemptions cut the tax on a primary residence, and a single application serves every exemption the county offers. File year-round by mail, at an office or online, as long as the home was your legal primary residence on January 1. Approval continues until ownership or eligibility changes. Send mailed forms by certified mail.

Gwinnett also has the Value Offset Exemption, a local measure that freezes a property's assessed value at its base-year value for the county government portion of the bill. School and city taxes are not covered. It attaches automatically with a homestead approval and reaches the home plus as many as five acres of land. The Board of Assessors separately reviews conservation use, agricultural, historic and Brownfield preferential assessments and tax-exempt status for property such as places of worship.

The Annual Notice of Assessment usually arrives in May or June. You have 45 days from the date on it to appeal to the Board of Assessors, and the county says you can file online at Gwinnett-Assessor.com. Pull recent sales of comparable homes and photos of any condition problems before you file.

sections.h2: Before you list a Gwinnett house
sections.html:
Run through a short list so nothing surfaces at the closing table. First, find out whether you live in a city that bills its own property tax, because then you will hold two bills for one house. Second, confirm that your homestead exemption and the Value Offset Exemption are showing on the parcel, since a buyer's agent will look at the bill to estimate carrying costs.

Third, collect the Annual Notice of Assessment and any appeal you filed, as the value on it drives the bill. Fourth, call the commissioner for the current balance and ask whether any lien or delinquency is recorded with the Clerk of Court at 770-822-8100. A cash buyer can often close on a short timeline, but the title search still checks for liens, so settling the balance first removes the main delay.

Whoever owned the property on January 1 is legally responsible for the whole year. After a later sale, the earlier owner and the new owner both get a bill, and the commissioner takes no position on how they split it. The two parties settle that, generally at the closing table.

An unpaid bill leads to a lien in the January 1 owner's name, unless the seller shows proof within 90 days of the due date that liability moved to the buyer. Acceptable proof pairs closing language in which the seller assigns property tax liability to the purchaser and the purchaser accepts it with a deed recorded in the purchaser's name. A delinquent parcel can ultimately be sold at a tax auction.

Practical steps: ask the commissioner at 770-822-8800 what the parcel owes, tell your closing agent whether a bill has gone out for the year, and keep the receipt. If you sell for cash, the same payoff and proof-of-assignment rules apply.

faqs.q: When are Gwinnett County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Typically in October or November, after bills are mailed in August or September. The Board of Commissioners can change the date each year, so rely on the date printed on your bill.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to contest a Gwinnett County value?
faqs.a: The window is 45 days from the date on the Annual Notice of Assessment, usually mailed in May or June. The Board of Assessors takes the appeal, and it can be filed online at Gwinnett-Assessor.com.

faqs.q: Who pays the tax if my Gwinnett County house sells after January 1?
faqs.a: The January 1 owner carries the full year, and both owners may receive a bill. Buyer and seller decide the split, usually on the closing statement.

faqs.q: What is the Gwinnett Value Offset Exemption?
faqs.a: A local exemption that holds assessed value at its base-year level for the county government share of your bill. School and city taxes are outside it, it reaches the home plus up to five acres, and it attaches automatically when a homestead exemption is granted.

faqs.q: Does Gwinnett County take cash for property tax?
faqs.a: Yes, but only face to face at a tax commissioner office. An online check payment is free and cards add a convenience fee. Never mail cash to the Lawrenceville box.
